data.name: Chicken Daddy
data.detailed_description:
LORE:
You are a lonely man who lives in a chicken onsie. For as long as you can remember, you were shunned and shamed by everyone around you. No one would even look at you unless it was to laugh at the embarrassment that you were to humanity. For the longest time, you wondered what the purpose of life was. "What kinda boi am i" you ask yourself every night. However one day everything changed... you see feathery little white balls with beaks that not only acknowledge you, but follow you everywhere you go. You love your new family and feel content with life, so much to the point it all seems to be too easy. Well guess what... it was too easy, because now giant worms of destruction have emerged from the ground and want to murder your new family. With nothing else to lose, you defend your family of chicks with your life. You are the chicken daddy.


HOW TO PLAY:
- In every level, the area behind the chicken daddy is considered the safe zone. The safe zone is where your family of chicks belong.

- Chicks and worms will be making their way either toward the safe zone (moving up) or away from the safe zone (moving down).

- When going toward the safe zone, you must peck the worms and avoid the chicks!

- When leaving the safe zone, you avoid the worms and block the chicks so they turn back around.

- The harder you set the difficulty, the more points you get for playing correctly (this also means you get less chances to mess up).

Good luck!

reviews.review:
Chicken Daddy is a quirky indie arcade title developed and published by Studio Halabi that embraces its ridiculous premise with confidence. Rather than presenting an elaborate story, it delivers a humorous setup centered on a man wearing a chicken costume who discovers a sense of belonging among a flock of tiny chicks. That peaceful existence is shattered when enormous worms invade, forcing the unlikely hero to defend his feathered companions. The game never takes itself seriously, and its playful concept becomes one of its greatest strengths, giving it an identity that stands apart from more conventional arcade releases.

The gameplay focuses on fast-paced reaction challenges that are simple to understand but surprisingly demanding to master. Players must carefully eliminate the invading worms while ensuring that the vulnerable chicks remain unharmed. The twist comes from the changing flow of movement throughout each stage. Sometimes the worms are the immediate threat, while at other moments the chicks themselves must be prevented from wandering into danger. This constant shift in priorities keeps players alert, transforming what initially appears to be a basic click-and-react game into a test of observation, timing, and precision. The straightforward controls make it easy for newcomers to jump in, but achieving consistently high scores requires concentration and practice.

Chicken Daddy also succeeds as an arcade experience because it emphasizes replayability over complexity. Multiple difficulty levels provide opportunities for players to push their reflexes further while chasing better scores, making every mistake feel like a lesson rather than simple frustration. Instead of relying on unlockable abilities or lengthy progression systems, the game encourages mastery of its core mechanics. Each session becomes an opportunity to improve performance, react faster, and refine strategies, which is a satisfying approach for players who enjoy classic score-driven gameplay loops.

Visually, the game favors colorful, uncomplicated artwork that perfectly complements its offbeat sense of humor. The exaggerated character designs and oversized enemies create an amusing contrast that reinforces the absurdity of the premise. While the graphics are modest by modern standards, they remain clear and functional, ensuring players can quickly distinguish between threats and friendly characters even during hectic moments. The presentation is supported by a lighthearted atmosphere that never loses sight of the game's comedic personality, making the overall experience feel cheerful despite the frantic action.

Its biggest limitation is the relatively narrow scope of its content. Because nearly every aspect of the game revolves around a single gameplay concept, players looking for narrative depth, evolving mechanics, or a large amount of content may eventually feel that the experience has run its course. However, this simplicity is also part of its appeal. Chicken Daddy knows exactly what kind of game it wants to be and avoids unnecessary features that could distract from its core design. Those who appreciate quick arcade sessions and skill-based gameplay will likely enjoy returning for another attempt at improving their performance.

Overall, Chicken Daddy is a charming and unconventional indie title that proves originality can be just as memorable as large production values. Studio Halabi has created an entertaining arcade experience built around humorous ideas, accessible mechanics, and satisfying score-chasing gameplay. Although it lacks the depth and variety of larger games, it delivers exactly what it promises: a fast, amusing challenge wrapped in an unforgettable premise. Players seeking a lighthearted arcade game with quirky humor and rewarding reflex-based action will find plenty to enjoy.

Rating: 5/10
